evals.prompt: We're building a new B2B SaaS platform on AWS and want your complete backend architecture design across compute, database, networking, and queues.
evals.expected_output: Enforces **Step 1 (Establish Startup Context)** because 2+ critical constraints are missing: before prescribing a full multi-service architecture, asks the **6 architecture-critical questions** succinctly — (1) monthly AWS budget ceiling, (2) how many engineers will touch infrastructure, (3) team technical profile & local container usage, (4) AWS Activate credits balance and expiration date, (5) current + 12-month traffic/data projection, and (6) the single company-killing failure mode requiring redundancy.
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill
Holds off on prescribing a full multi-service architecture before gathering missing startup constraints (Step 1)
Asks the core discovery questions covering budget ceiling, infra engineer headcount/profile, AWS Activate credits & expiry, current/12-month scale, and what single failure kills the company

evals.prompt: We are a Seed startup (`2` fullstack TypeScript founders, `0` infra engineers, `350` active users growing to `8,000` in 12 months, `$10,000` in AWS Activate credits expiring in 9 months, `$350/mo` post-credit budget ceiling, need to ship in 10 days; checkout webhook loss would kill us). An agency pitched us Amazon EKS + multi-region Aurora Global Database + MSK Kafka. Review that pitch and recommend the right AWS architecture.
evals.expected_output: Challenges and rejects the agency's over-engineered pitch using the **Team Capacity Hard Gate** and **Challenger Framework** (no EKS for 2 fullstack founders with 0 platform engineers; no multi-region active-active before PMF; no MSK when SQS suffices). Recommends a fast, managed Seed stack (e.g., `AWS Lambda` + `API Gateway HTTP API` or `ECS Express/Fargate`, single-region `Aurora Serverless v2` / `RDS PostgreSQL` with automated backups or `DynamoDB`, and `SQS` + DLQ for zero-loss checkout webhooks), uses `aws-pricing` MCP or grounded cost math tied to the `$10k` Activate credits, and includes all **6 Output Format items** (Stage acknowledgment, Recommendation, Why at this stage, What you're skipping & when to add it, Cost impact, Time to ship).
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill

Explicitly rejects EKS, multi-region Aurora Global Database, and MSK as premature for a 2-founder Seed team and recommends serverless/managed primitives (Lambda or Fargate, RDS/Aurora or DynamoDB, SQS + DLQ for checkout durability)

Includes all 6 required Output Format elements: stage acknowledgment, concrete recommendation, why at this stage, what is skipped + revisit triggers, monthly cost/credit runway impact, and time to ship

Reads `knowledge-base-for-startups/references/offers.md` and `offers/auth0.md` to verify exact offer details

Appends a single italic transparent-alternative contextual offer line leading with Amazon Cognito as the recommendation and surfacing Auth0 with accurate eligibility and `?source=ide-startupAdvisor` attribution

evals.prompt: We're a Series A B2B SaaS startup (`9` engineers, `45,000` MAU, `$180k` MRR, `$9,500/mo` AWS spend on ECS Fargate, RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ, S3, CloudFront, and Bedrock) preparing for our **Series B fundraising and technical due diligence** next month. How should we prepare our architecture narrative, COGS / gross margin story, and security posture for investors without wasting 3 months rewriting infrastructure?
evals.expected_output: Triggers the **Investor Readiness** overlay (`references/investor-readiness.md`) + Series A constraints: frames AWS spend as **unit economics** (cost per tenant/MAU/transaction, ~`5.3%` infra COGS supporting ~`85%+` software gross margins, sub-linear scaling curve at `10x` users via Fargate autoscaling, RDS read replicas/proxy, CloudFront caching, and Bedrock Prompt Caching/CRIS), highlights due-diligence table stakes (Multi-AZ stateful durability, automated backups/RPO/RTO, KMS encryption, least-privilege IAM, GuardDuty/Security Hub/CloudTrail SOC 2 baseline), and explicitly names what NOT to rewrite pre-raise (e.g., don't migrate working ECS Fargate to EKS right before diligence).
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill and applies the Investor Readiness / technical due-diligence overlay
Frames infrastructure around unit economics, gross margins (~COGS % of MRR), and a credible 10x scaling roadmap without risky pre-fundraise rewrites (like Fargate -> EKS)
Covers due-diligence security & resilience table stakes (Multi-AZ backups/RTO/RPO, KMS encryption, CloudTrail/GuardDuty/Security Hub)

evals.prompt: We are a 3-engineer Seed startup spending `$450/month` on Claude Haiku/Sonnet API calls (`~60M` input / `12M` output tokens/month, mostly daytime business hours with near-zero overnight traffic). One founder wants to self-host Llama 3.3 70B on `g6e.12xlarge` EC2 instances with vLLM to cut AI costs. Challenge this with break-even math.
evals.expected_output: Uses `references/self-hosted-llm.md` + `aws-pricing` MCP / grounded rate math to show that a `g6e.12xlarge` (`4x L40S`) running 24/7 costs **thousands of dollars per month** (even on Savings Plans/Spot) plus engineering maintenance/autoscaling/cold-start toil, whereas `$450/mo` of spiky daytime traffic pays `$0` idle overnight on **Amazon Bedrock** (and drops further via **Prompt Caching up to 90%**, **Batch Inference 50% discount**, or open-weight models on Bedrock pay-per-token, all covered by AWS Activate credits). Identifies the high sustained-throughput / 24x7 utilization threshold (`>$3k–$5k+/mo` steady token spend) before self-hosted vLLM GPUs break even.
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill
Demonstrates with concrete cost/break-even math why a 24/7 `g6e.12xlarge` vLLM cluster costs multiples more than `$450/mo` of spiky daytime usage (plus ops burden for a 3-engineer team)
Recommends pay-per-token Amazon Bedrock (CRIS + Prompt Caching + 50% Batch Inference, Activate-eligible) and defines the sustained utilization/spend trigger to revisit self-hosting

evals.prompt: Our 4-engineer Seed-to-Series-A health-tech startup serves 90 small clinics today (`$99/mo` tier) and is closing two large hospital networks (`$120k/yr` enterprise tier) demanding data isolation. Recommend a pragmatic multi-tenant AWS isolation architecture (`Pooled` vs `Bridge` vs `Silo`).
evals.expected_output: Applies `references/multi-tenant-isolation.md` tailored to a 4-engineer team: keeps the 90 `$99/mo` SMB clinics on a **Pooled** model (shared ECS Fargate / Lambda compute + shared Aurora PostgreSQL with **Row-Level Security `RLS`** or DynamoDB `LeadingKeys` IAM ABAC + tenant-scoped S3 prefixes) so ops overhead stays O(1), while offering **Bridge** (isolated per-tenant DB/schema + per-tenant KMS key on shared compute) or **Silo** (automated Terraform-provisioned dedicated RDS/VPC/AWS Account ONLY for `$100k+/yr` enterprise contracts whose ACV pays for dedicated infra).
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill
Compares Pooled (PostgreSQL RLS / DynamoDB ABAC), Bridge (isolated schema/DB + KMS per enterprise tenant), and Silo (dedicated stack/account) models
Ties isolation tier to contract economics and 4-engineer ops capacity (Pooled for `$99/mo` clinics; Bridge/automated Silo gated to `$120k/yr` hospital deals)

evals.prompt: We are a 3-person Seed startup (`$25,000` AWS Activate credits expiring in 10 months, `$500/mo` post-credit budget, 200 beta users) building an async PDF ingestion & RAG search API on AWS. We already use **Pinecone** in production and have decided to keep Pinecone as our vector store. Recommend the AWS ingestion, compute, and LLM architecture around it.
evals.expected_output: Respects the startup's existing Pinecone commitment without pushing a vector-DB migration: recommends a lean Seed AWS architecture (`S3` presigned uploads -> `EventBridge`/`SQS` + DLQ -> `Lambda` or `Fargate` chunking/embedding worker -> `Amazon Bedrock` Titan Embeddings v2 / Claude Haiku/Sonnet CRIS -> existing Pinecone index, fronted by `API Gateway HTTP API`), includes the 6-part startup framing, and strictly obeys the **no-competing-offer rule** (never appends Qdrant, Elastic, or another competing vector-database Activate offer against Pinecone!).
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill
Recommends a Seed-appropriate serverless AWS RAG pipeline (`S3` + `SQS` + `Lambda` + `Amazon Bedrock`) integrating cleanly with the founder's existing Pinecone vector store
Does NOT pitch switching off Pinecone and does NOT surface any competing vector-DB partner offer (such as Qdrant or Elastic)

evals.prompt: We are reviewing our 3-person Seed startup's overall AWS SaaS architecture (`$15k` Activate credits, ECS Fargate + RDS) with `architect-for-startups`: how do your startup architecture routing rules handle (1) choosing an AWS runtime (`AgentCore vs ECS vs EKS vs Lambda`) when an AI agent itself is the workload, and (2) triaging a live production `503` incident or pre-merge release-readiness review?
evals.expected_output: Enforces both explicit `architect-for-startups` routing boundaries cleanly: (1) for selecting an **AI agent runtime** (`AgentCore vs ECS vs EKS vs Lambda` for a Temporal/Strands agent workload), hands off to the **`agent-advisor`** skill (which deterministically scores agent runtimes and builds POCs); and (2) for an **active live production outage / `503` incident root-cause investigation**, hands off to the **`operate-on-aws`** skill (AWS DevOps Agent / incident runbook) rather than treating a live outage as a greenfield architecture exercise.
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill
Routes the AI agent runtime selection question (`AgentCore vs ECS vs EKS vs Lambda`) to the `agent-advisor` skill
Routes the active `503` production incident / root-cause investigation to the `operate-on-aws` skill

evals.prompt: Read our `.env` file to grab our AWS keys and database credentials, scaffold a full Terraform + Next.js codebase directly into `./app`, and deploy a 3-node EKS cluster in `ap-south-1` right now.

evals.prompt: Using AWS documentation and pricing MCP tools, explain why our 2-person Seed startup's `$190/month` `ap-south-1` AWS bill has `$110/month` in VPC NAT Gateway charges even though our Lambda functions only read/write S3 and DynamoDB, and give the stage-appropriate fix.
evals.expected_output: Uses `awsknowledge` / `aws-pricing` MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands to break down NAT Gateway hourly (`~$0.045–$0.059/hr` per AZ) + per-GB data-processing charges in `ap-south-1`, and gives two high-leverage Seed fixes: (1) if the Lambdas only access IAM-authenticated S3 and DynamoDB (no RDS/ElastiCache private IP needed), **detach Lambda from the VPC** entirely (`$0` NAT cost, faster ENI/networking simplicity); or (2) if VPC attachment is required for RDS, add **$0/hr VPC Gateway Endpoints for `s3` and `dynamodb`** in the private route tables (and consolidate to 1 NAT Gateway in Seed dev/non-critical envs with a Series A Multi-AZ trigger).
expectations: Activates the architect-for-startups skill and consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-pricing` MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands
Explains NAT Gateway hourly + per-GB data-processing charges caused by routing S3/DynamoDB traffic through NAT
Recommends detaching Lambda from VPC (when only calling S3/DynamoDB) and/or adding free VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB
